(p-٤٩٦)Surat al-Talaq (The Divorce)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾. He addressed the Prophet ﷺ specifically in the call but used the plural in the address, because the Prophet is the leader (imam) of his community and its exemplar (qudwa), as one says to the chief of a people: "O so-and-so, do such-and-such," to show his precedence and to recognize his leadership, and that he is the exemplar of his people. So he alone stands in the ruling for all of them and takes the place of all of them. It has also been said that the implied wording is: "O Prophet and the believers." The meaning of "when you divorce women" is: when you intend to divorce them and resolve to do so. This follows the principle of treating one who is about to undertake a matter and is approaching it as though he has already begun it, as in his ﷺ saying: "Whoever kills an enemy, he shall have his spoils." From this principle, one who is walking to prayer and one who is waiting for it are treated as one who is praying.

﴿So divorce them for their 'iddah (waiting period)﴾. Divorce them while facing toward their 'iddah. In the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ it is: "in the beginning of their 'iddah" (fi qubuli 'iddatihinna). When a woman is divorced during the purity (tuhr) that precedes her first qur' (menstrual period, lit. "period" or "interval," used of both purity and menstruation) of her periods, she has been divorced at the start of her 'iddah. What is meant is that women who have been consummated and who observe 'iddah by menstruation should be divorced during a purity in which they have not had intercourse, and then left alone until their 'iddah ends. This is the best form of divorce.

﴿And count the 'iddah﴾. Keep precise count of it and complete it as three full periods, beginning from the moment of divorce, with no shortfall in them. The address is to the husbands, because women tend to be negligent (in this).

(p-٤٩٧)﴿And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them﴾ until their 'iddah has ended,

﴿from their houses﴾, from the dwellings in which they lived before the 'iddah. These are the husbands' houses, and they are ascribed to the women because they are specifically theirs in respect of residence. This indicates that providing residence (sukna) is obligatory, and that breaking an oath (hinth) by entering a house in which so-and-so lives, without its being owned by him, applies to someone who swore not to enter "his house." The meaning of "expulsion" is that the husbands should not expel them out of anger toward them, or out of dislike for living with them, or because they themselves need the dwellings, and that they should not permit the women to leave when they ask to do so, indicating that the husbands' permission has no effect in lifting the prohibition.

﴿And they [the women] should not go out﴾ on their own initiative, if they wish to do so,

﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾. It has been said that this is adultery, meaning: unless they commit adultery, in which case they may go out to have the legal punishment (hadd) carried out on them. It has also been said that her leaving before the end of the 'iddah is itself an immorality.

﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾, that is, the rulings mentioned above.

﴿Whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know﴾, O addressee,

﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some new matter﴾, by turning his heart from hatred of her to love of her, from aversion to desire for her, and from resolve to divorce to regret over it, so that he takes her back. The meaning is: "So divorce them for their 'iddah and count the 'iddah, and do not expel them from their houses, perhaps you will regret it and take them back."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 2:

﴿When they have reached their term﴾, that is, they have come close to the end of the ʿidda (the waiting period),

﴿then retain them honourably or part from them honourably﴾, meaning: you have the choice. If you wish, there is ar-rajʿa (the taking back of the wife during the waiting period) and retention in kindness and goodness; and if you wish, there is abandoning the return and separation, and avoiding harm (ḍirār), which is that a man takes his wife back at the end of her ʿidda and then divorces her again, to lengthen the ʿidda upon her and to torment her.

﴿And call to witness﴾, meaning at the time of the return and at the time of the separation, both together. This calling of witnesses is recommended (mandūb), so that no denial (tajāḥud) arises between them.

﴿two just men from among you﴾, from among the Muslims,

﴿and establish the testimony for God﴾, sincerely for His sake. This means that they establish it not for the one in whose favour it is given, nor against the one against whom it is given, nor for any worldly purpose, other than establishing the truth and averting harm.

﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾, the exhortation to establish the testimony for the sake of God and for the purpose of upholding justice (qist).

﴿by which is admonished whoever believes in God and the Last Day﴾, meaning: only those people benefit from it.

﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out﴾. This is a parenthetical clause (jumla iʿtirāḍiyya) confirming what preceded concerning carrying out the matter of divorce in accordance with the Sunna. The meaning is: "Whoever fears God, divorces according to the Sunna, does not harm the woman in her ʿidda, does not expel her from her dwelling, takes precaution, and calls witnesses, God will make for him a way out from the distresses and the narrow straits that come with matters concerning spouses, will relieve him of them, and will grant him deliverance."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 3:

﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾, from a direction that does not occur to his mind and that he does not anticipate. It is permissible that this be mentioned by way of digression (istitrad) when mentioning His saying: "﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]", meaning: "And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out (makhraj) and a deliverance (makhlas) from the distresses (ghumum) of this world and the Hereafter." It is also related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited it and said: "A way out from the doubts (shubuhat) of this world, from the agonies (ghamarat) of death, and from the hardships (shada'id) of the Day of Resurrection." And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know a verse which, if people adopted it, would suffice them: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ [al-Talaq: 4]." So he continued reciting it and repeating it.

It is also narrated that the polytheists captured the son of Awf ibn Malik. He came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My son has been captured," and he complained to him of poverty. He said: "There remains in the household of Muhammad nothing but a mudd. So fear Allah and be patient, and recite much: (There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty)." So he returned to his home and said to his wife: "The Messenger of Allah has commanded me and you to recite much: 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty.'" She said: "How excellent is what he has commanded us!" So they both began to say that. While he was in his house, his son knocked on the door, and with him were a hundred camels which the enemy had overlooked, so he had driven them off. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾, entrusting his affair to Him, free from hope in others and from managing his own self,

﴿then He is sufficient for him﴾, sufficient for him in both abodes,

﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾, according to Hafs, meaning: He will carry out His command. Others read "bālighun amrahu", meaning: He reaches what He wills; no aim escapes Him and no sought object overcomes Him, (p-499)

﴿Allah has already set for everything a measure﴾, a determination (taqdir) and a appointed time (tawqit). This is an explanation of the obligation of relying upon Allah and entrusting the matter to Him, because when it is known that every portion of provision and the like comes about only by His determination and appointed time, nothing remains but submission to the decree (qadar) and reliance.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 4:

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation - if you have doubt, then their waiting period is three months; and those who have not menstruated [likewise].﴾ It is narrated that some people said: "We know the waiting period of women who have courses (qur', i.e. menstrual periods), so what is the waiting period of those who have not menstruated?" Then this was revealed.

﴿If you have doubt﴾ means: their ruling has become unclear to you, and you do not know how they should observe their waiting period.

﴿Then their waiting period is three months﴾ means: this is their ruling. It has also been said: "If you have doubt" concerns the blood of adult women who have reached the limit of despair - and they have estimated that limit as sixty years, and as fifty-five years - whether it is blood of menstruation or of istihadah (irregular bleeding); then their waiting period is three months. And if this is the waiting period of the woman about whom there is doubt, then the woman about whom there is no doubt is more deserving of it.

﴿And those who have not menstruated﴾ are the young girls. Its implied meaning is: "And those who have not menstruated, their waiting period is three months," and the clause was omitted because what has been mentioned indicates it.

﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is﴾ - their waiting period - ﴿that they lay down their burden.﴾ The text covers divorced women and widows. It is narrated from ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The waiting period of a pregnant woman whose husband has died is the longer of the two terms."

﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾ - He will make his affair easy for him and loosen his difficulties, because of taqwa (God-consciousness).

﴿That is the command of Allah﴾, i.e., what has been known of the ruling concerning these women observing the waiting period (ʿiddah),

﴿which He has sent down to you﴾, from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz),

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾, by acting upon what He has sent down of these rulings and by preserving the rights that are obligatory upon him,

﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds and will enlarge for him his reward﴾. Then he explained taqwa (God-consciousness) in his saying, "﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾," as if it were said: "How do we act with taqwa regarding the women observing the waiting period?" So it was said:

(p-٥٠٠) ﴿Lodge them﴾, and so forth,

﴿where you dwell﴾: here "min" is partitive (al-tab'idiyyah), and its object is omitted. The meaning is: "Lodge them in a place from where you dwell," that is, in part of your dwelling place.

﴿according to your means﴾: this is an explanatory apposition (ʿatf bayan) to his saying "where you dwell," and an elaboration of it, as if it were said: "Lodge them in a place from your dwelling that you are able to afford." Al-wujd means capacity and ability. It has been read with all three vowel patterns, but the well-known reading is with a ḍammah. Maintenance (nafaqah) and lodging (sukna) are obligatory for every divorced woman. According to Malik and al-Shafi'i, a woman who has been irrevocably divorced (al-mabtutah) has no maintenance, based on the hadith of Fatima bint Qays, that her husband irrevocably divorced her, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You have no right to lodging or maintenance." And from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him): "We will not abandon the Book of our Lord and the Sunnah of our Prophet for the word of a woman, who may have forgotten, or been mistaken. I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'She is entitled to lodging and maintenance.'"

﴿And do not harm them﴾: do not treat them with harm.

﴿to constrain them﴾: within the dwelling, by means of some devices, such as placing in it someone who is not agreeable to them, or who occupies their space, or other such things, until you force them to leave.

﴿And if they are﴾: that is, the divorced women,

﴿pregnant﴾: those who carry children.

﴿then spend on them until they give birth﴾: the purpose of stipulating pregnancy is that the period of pregnancy may be long, so that someone might think maintenance falls away once the length of the pregnant woman's waiting period has passed. That misconception is therefore negated.

﴿And if they nurse for you﴾: that is, these divorced women, if they nurse a child for you, whether from others or from among themselves, after the bond of marriage has ended.

﴿then give them their wages﴾: their ruling in this matter is the ruling of wet nurses (al-azhar), and it is not permissible to hire them if the child is theirs, as long as they have not separated from him, contrary to al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him).

﴿And confer among yourselves﴾: that is, consult with one another by mutual agreement about the wage, or let some of you enjoin others. Or the address is to the fathers and mothers.

﴿in kindness﴾: in what is fitting to the Sunnah and good in manliness. So the father should not haggle, and the mother should not be obstinate, because it is their child, and both share in it, and in the obligation of compassion toward him.

﴿And if you disagree﴾: you become constrained, so the mother does not agree to what a stranger nurses for, and the father does not increase beyond that. (p-٥٠١) ﴿then another woman will nurse for him﴾: another will be found, and a nurse other than the mother will not be lacking to nurse him. This contains an element of reproach to the mother for her obstinacy. His saying "for him" means for the father: the father will find someone other than an obstinate woman who will nurse his child if his mother is obstinate with him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 7:

﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him.﴾ That is: let each one of them, the affluent and the straitened, spend to the extent of his capacity, meaning what he has been commanded to spend on divorced women and nursing mothers. The phrase "whose provision is restricted" (qudira ʿalayhi rizquh) means it was narrowed, i.e., Allah has provided for him according to his means.

﴿Allah does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it,﴾ that is, beyond what He has given it of provision.

﴿Allah will bring about ease after hardship,﴾ that is, after constriction in livelihood, abundance. This is a promise to the one in hardship of ease.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 65, verse 8:

﴿And how many a town﴾: that is, the people of a town.

﴿rebelled﴾: that is, disobeyed

﴿against the command of their Lord and His messengers﴾: they turned away from it, out of arrogance (ʿutuww) and obstinacy.

﴿So We called it to account with a severe reckoning﴾: with thorough scrutiny and close examination.

﴿And We punished it with a dreadful punishment﴾: "nukuran" is read with the damma on the nun and the kaf (nukur) by Madani and Abu Bakr; it means a great, terrible (munkar) punishment.

﴿So they tasted the evil consequence of their affair, and the outcome of their affair was loss (khusran)﴾. That is: loss (khasaran) and ruin (halakan). What is meant is the reckoning of the Hereafter and its punishment, and what they taste in it of evil consequence and encounter of loss. It is expressed in the past tense (al-madi) because what is awaited of Allah's promise and threat is, in reality, already met, and what is certain to occur is as though it has already occurred.

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾. This repeats the threat and clarifies that it is awaited, as if he said: Allah has prepared for them this punishment.

﴿So fear Allah, O people of understanding, you who have believed﴾. So let that be for you, O people of understanding among the believers, a means of grace (lutf) in fearing Allah and dreading His punishment. It is also permissible that what is meant is the counting of their misdeeds and the full accounting of them against them in this world, and their recording in the pages of the recording angels (al-Hafaza), and the punishment they suffered in the present life. It is also permissible that "they tasted" (ʿatat) and what is conjoined to it be an attribute of the town, and that "Allah has prepared for them" be the response (jawab) to "how many" (kaʾayyin), which is a grammatical term for a construction meaning "how many," whose sentence requires a response.

﴿Allah has sent down to you a reminder﴾, that is, the Qur'an. (p-502)

and the word "rasulan" (a messenger) is in the accusative by a verb implied in the sentence, its estimated form being: "He sent a messenger" (arsala rasulan); or it is a substitute (badal) for "dhikran", as if he were himself a reminder (dhikr); or it is according to an estimate of an omitted modifier, meaning: "Indeed Allah has sent down to you one possessing a reminder (dhikr), a messenger"; or "dhikr" is intended to mean honour (sharaf), as in His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 44], meaning: "one of honour and glory with Allah." And by "the messenger" is meant Jibril, or Muhammad, peace be upon them both.

﴿Reciting﴾, that is, the messenger, or Allah, Mighty and Majestic,

﴿the clear signs of Allah, so that He may bring out﴾, Allah,

﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, that is: so that there may be realized for them what they are presently upon of faith and righteous action; or so that He may bring out those whom He knew would believe,

﴿from darknesses into light﴾, from the darknesses of disbelief, or ignorance, into the light of faith, or knowledge.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds, He will admit him﴾, and with the nun, it is read by Madani and Shami,

﴿into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾. He used the singular and the plural, taking it according to the wording of "man" and according to its meaning.

﴿Allah has indeed made good provision for him﴾. In it is the sense of wonder and magnification of what Allah has provided the believers of reward.

God, who created seven heavens — this is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is "seven heavens." The exegetes are unanimous that the heavens are seven.

"And of the earth, the like of them" — in the accusative (bi'l-nasb), coordinated (ma'tuf) upon "seven heavens." It has been said: there is no verse in the Qur'an that indicates the earths are seven except this verse. And between every two heavens is a distance of five hundred years, and the thickness of each heaven is likewise; and the earths are like the heavens. It has also been said: the earth is one, but the climes (aqalim) are seven.

"The command descends between them" — that is, God's command and decree proceed between them, and His dominion takes effect within them.

"That you may know that God is powerful over everything" — the lam (of purpose, lam al-ta'lil) is connected to "created" (khalaqa).

"And that God has encompassed all things in knowledge" — here "'ilman" is a tamyiz (specification), or it is a verbal noun (masdar) not from the same root as the first verb, meaning: "He has known every thing with knowledge."
